messages:
bob_customer: Hey team, we're seeing a batch of embedding calls start failing this morning after a config change. Calls used to return 1536-dim vectors, now some responses are 1024 and our indexer throws a dimension-mismatch error. Example curl we used:

bob_customer: ```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-org-XXXX' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"input":"hello world"}'
```

bob_customer: We didn't explicitly set a model param — relied on default project mapping. No config changes on our side except rotating keys last night. Any ideas? :confused:

alice_support: Sorry for the interruption, Bob. Can you paste the full request headers (with keys redacted) and one example response body that shows the 1024 vector? Also which SDK/version if any.

bob_customer: Pasted. We use their node SDK v2.4 but also have some curl tests. Header snippet (redacted):

bob_customer: ```
Authorization: Bearer sk-org-XXXX
X-Project-ID: proj-abc
X-Org-ID: org-123
Content-Type: application/json
```

bob_customer: Response (trimmed):

bob_customer: ```json
{"data":[{"embedding":[0.003, -0.12, /* ... total 1024 floats ... */], "model":"text-embed-small-v1"}], "model":"text-embed-small-v1"}
```

alice_support: OK that's helpful. Previously you got 1536-dim from `text-embed-large-v1` right?

bob_customer: Exactly. Our indexer expects 1536. The rotation last night swapped an org-scoped key. We suspect the platform selected a different default model after key rotation.

automation_bot: Incident detection alert: spike in embedding-dim-mismatch for project proj-abc starting 2026-02-22T08:34:00Z (+120 errors/min).

alice_support: I'm escalating to eng-runtime and eng-ml. @carmen_eng_ml @dan_eng_runtime can you take a look at model selection when both org and project headers are present?

carmen_eng_ml: Looking now. Quick question: does your code ever set a `model` param in the request body? If not, runtime chooses a model based on key-to-default mapping.

bob_customer: No explicit model param. Historically project mapping pointed to `text-embed-large-v1` (1536). After the key swap the responses show `text-embed-small-v1` (1024).

dan_eng_runtime: Reproduced locally by sending an org-scoped key + X-Project-ID header. It looks like a recent change to header precedence (PR #2389) made org-level API keys take precedence over project defaults when no `model` is specified. That would explain why your org key maps to a different default embedding model.

carmen_eng_ml: Right — org keys are associated with an org-wide default model in our metadata table. Project mappings were meant to override, but the precedence switch flipped in the runtime selector. That's a bug.

alice_support: Is this a one-off misroute or could keys cause other projects to get wrong model variants?

dan_eng_runtime: Potentially affects any request without explicit `model`. If a customer rotates in an org-scoped key that belongs to an org with a different default model, their projects might get the org default.

bob_customer: This explains the failures. Our pipeline batches embeddings assuming 1536 floats; the runtime returned 1024 and the indexer rejected the vectors. Throughput dropped because batch job retries.

carmen_eng_ml: Short-term mitigation: explicitly pass `model: "text-embed-large-v1"` in your payload or switch to a project-scoped key. We'll also add a quick server-side validation to return 400 if returned embedding dims != expected dims for the model advertised.

alice_support: Can you share the exact payload to force the model param?

bob_customer: Sure, we'll test:```
POST /v1/embeddings
{
  "model": "text-embed-large-v1",
  "input": ["a","b"]
}
```

bob_customer: Tested — forcing model works, indexer accepts 1536 vectors again. Throughput restored. Thanks. :thumbsup:

elaine_account: Noted for billing/contracting — project mapping change could affect unit pricing (large vs small). We should notify affected customers if we roll the fix.

carmen_eng_ml: Root cause summary: PR #2389 inadvertently changed model selection precedence so org-key defaults override project-level defaults when no explicit `model` is set. Fix plan: revert precedence to project-over-org in runtime selector (hotfix roll), add unit tests, and add defensive validation that returns a helpful error when embedding dims don't match advertised model.

dan_eng_runtime: Hotfix rollout started to canary (region us-west2) at 2026-02-22T09:10Z. We'll monitor error rate and metrics. If green, promote globally in 30m.

automation_bot: Deploy event: canary deploy started for runtime-selector-hotfix by dan_eng_runtime at 2026-02-22T09:11:42Z.

alice_support: Bob — we've rolled canary; can you confirm no more 1024 responses for your project?

bob_customer: Confirmed. No 1024 responses in last 10 minutes. Batch jobs completed successfully. Big relief.

alice_support: Follow-ups: (1) We'll ship a patch that returns 400 with an explicit message when dims mismatch (2) We'll add telemetry to alert if a project's observed model deviates from its mapping (3) Elaine will draft customer comms for any affected accounts.

elaine_account: I'll prepare a short email + in-console banner for any customers who saw the mismatch. Recommend offering cost offset if we caused unexpected higher-cost model usage.

carmen_eng_ml: Also adding an integration test that simulates org vs project keys to prevent regressions. Tracking issue: RD-ISSUE-1456.

alice_support: Thanks everyone. Bob, we'll keep this thread updated if anything else pops up. Appreciate the quick repro details.

bob_customer: Thank you all for the fast turnaround.

automation_bot: Incident resolved: embedding-dim-mismatch for proj-abc reduced to baseline at 2026-02-22T09:42:03Z.
